description: reconcileProvisionalDisbursement (skills/economy/lending/lib/lending-verify.mjs:150-164) and its caller resolveStaleProvisioning (skills/economy/lending/lib/lending-orchestrator.mjs:117-138) still lack the SAME cross-ledger anti-replay guard this exact codebase already ships for the structurally identical hazard in verifyRepayment (lending-verify.mjs:84-86, `alreadyCredited = loanRows.some(row => row.tx_hash === txHash)`, explicitly documented as resolving FIND-202: 'same-loan OR cross-loan replay'). FIND-101's fix (iteration-2) made reconcileProvisionalDisbursement require the matched Transfer log's own VALUE to exactly equal loanRow.principal_usd -- but it never checks whether that log's own txHash has ALREADY been recorded (via extractTxHash) against a DIFFERENT loan_id anywhere in loans.jsonl. resolveStaleProvisioning (lending-orchestrator.mjs:124) calls `reconcile({ loanRow: staleRow })` -- it never passes `loanRows` (which it already has in scope as its own second parameter) into the reconcile call, and reconcileProvisionalDisbursement's own signature (`{loanRow, rpcUrl, fromBlock, toBlock}`) has no parameter to receive it even if it were passed. This is exploitable specifically BECAUSE of this exact protocol's own value structure: computeLoanCapUsd (lending-gate.mjs:134-145) returns a FLAT $0.02 for every cold-start attempt to a borrower with zero successful on-time repayments (0.02 * 2^0), so EVERY repeat loan attempt to the SAME struggling borrower -- the mainline retry pattern this exact reconciliation machinery exists to support, not a remote edge case -- shares the IDENTICAL wallet pair AND the IDENTICAL exact-match value FIND-101's own fix now trusts. Concrete chain (compounds with REQ-120's OWN documented false-negative risk, which the spec itself already acknowledges is possible -- specs/behavioral-spec.md:138-151): loan_N genuinely broadcasts but its OWN reconciliation attempt returns a false negative (e.g. eth_getLogs eventual-consistency lag, or any cause) and is wrongly marked disbursement_failed; the SAME borrower (not blocked -- isBorrowerEligible's hasOpenLoan check at lending-gate.mjs:113-116 only excludes status active/defaulted, never disbursement_failed/disbursement_uncertain) becomes eligible again; loan_N+1 is provisioned at the SAME $0.02 cap to the SAME wallet pair and itself gets stuck; the NEXT reconciliation attempt (for loan_N+1) scans the SAME lookback window, finds loan_N's own genuine, already-real, but never-locally-credited transfer (exact value + exact wallet-pair match), and incorrectly marks loan_N+1 'active' using loan_N's OWN txHash -- while loan_N sits permanently mis-recorded as disbursement_failed despite the borrower having actually received that principal. This is a real fund-misattribution/double-accounting outcome, not a UI nit, and it becomes live starting with THIS review's own imminent first fresh disbursement (loan_Franklin_2, same $0.02, same Franklin/Franklin2 pair, per the wake-gate.test.mjs REQ-118 recovery fixture's own confirmed shape).
testGap: skills/economy/lending/lib/__tests__/lending-verify.test.mjs's FIND-101 tests (lines 257-298) only ever exercise a SINGLE candidate loanRow against mocked logs of matching/non-matching VALUE -- no fixture ever supplies a `loanRows` ledger containing an ALREADY-active/repaid row whose own tx_hash equals the matched log's txHash, so reconcileProvisionalDisbursement's missing cross-row replay check is untested. skills/economy/lending/lib/__tests__/lending-orchestrator.test.mjs's resolveStaleProvisioning/FIND-102 tests (lines 377-435) never assert loanRows is forwarded into the reconcile() call, and no fixture proves a stale row's reconciliation is REJECTED when the matched transfer's txHash already appears against a different loan_id elsewhere in the ledger.
recommendation: Mirror verifyRepayment's own already-proven fix (FIND-202): (1) pass `loanRows` from resolveStaleProvisioning into reconcile({loanRow: staleRow, loanRows}); (2) extend reconcileProvisionalDisbursement's signature to accept loanRows and reject (`{found:false}`) any matched log whose own extractTxHash(...) value already equals some OTHER row's tx_hash in loanRows (same-loan OR cross-loan, exactly like verifyRepayment:84-86) before ever returning `{found:true, txHash}`.
